values.binNote: The bin does not store this bonus as a separate flat/ratio pair; instead VayneCondemn.StunDamage=1.5 is a multiplier applied to the full TotalDamage (base+0.5xbonusAD) via EmpoweredDamageTT = TotalDamage*1.5, i.e. the terrain-collision hit replaces the base hit with 1.5x its damage rather than adding a distinct extra instance. The wiki instead presents this as an additional 'bonus' component (50%*1.5 base, 25% bonusAD extra ratio) on top of the base hit so total = base hit + bonus hit = TotalDamage*2.5. The values here are the wiki's stated bonus-only numbers (0.5x base, 0.25 bonusAD coef), derived as 1.5x-1x of the base formula; the bin encodes the same total via a single multiplier rather than an additive bonus term.

primitives.note: Tumble arms next basic attack within 3s to deal bonus physical damage and reset attack timer

Silver Bolts stacks are applied by on-hit attacks and Condemn
3 stacks (each refreshing on reapplication, 3.5s duration) consumed on the 3rd to deal bonus true damage based on target max HP, min floor
Condemn deals physical damage on hit after a 0.25s cast/travel delay, on a mana-gated cooldown
Condemn's bonus damage + stun only trigger if the knocked-back target collides with terrain, which a dummy fight does not have unless assumed

Night Hunter is pure movement speed, never read by a damage sim

needsBespoke.why: Every mechanical piece (Tumble empowered-attack/reset, Silver Bolts on-hit stacking true damage, Condemn plain-cast physical damage with a terrain-conditional bonus, Final Hour timed self-buff plus cooldown manipulation, Night Hunter as pure defensive movement) maps onto existing primitives. The only open item is how to treat Condemn's terrain-collision bonus damage given the dummy fight has no terrain, which is an unsettled question, not a missing primitive.

unsettled.question: Does Condemn's terrain-collision bonus damage (stun + extra physical damage, doubling the hit to ~2.5x total) ever trigger in a stationary-dummy fight with no terrain behind the target?
options: Never triggers: dummy fight has no terrain, so Condemn only ever deals its base Damage (VayneCondemn.Damage + 0.5x bonus AD)
Simulator should assume terrain is present behind the dummy (a common competitive setup) so Condemn always lands the terrain bonus, dealing the full 2.5x/150% bonus AD total
quotes: If the target collides with [[terrain]], they take {{ccs|{{as|'''bonus''' physical damage}}|physical}} and become {{tip|stun|stunned}} for {{ap|1.5}} seconds.

unsettled.question: Does Tumble's bonus damage (on the empowered next attack) count as a separate damage instance from the basic attack it rides on, for the purposes of applying Silver Bolts on-hit stacking and any on-hit item effects?
options: Single combined attack event: the empowered attack (base AD + Tumble bonus) counts as one on-hit application, adding one Silver Bolts stack
Two separate instances: the basic-attack-tagged portion and the spell-damage-tagged bonus portion are distinct, potentially each triggering separate on-hit/on-cast interactions
quotes: The basic attack portion of ''Tumble's'' damage is tagged as {{tip|basic damage}} and {{tip|spell damage}}, while the bonus damage is tagged as {{tip|spell damage}}.

unsettled.question: Does casting Condemn (which also applies a Silver Bolts stack) count toward Silver Bolts' 3-stack threshold as its own instance separate from on-hit attacks, and can it itself consume/trigger the true-damage proc if it is the 3rd application?
options: Condemn applies a stack like any other application (refresh/increment) and can trigger the proc as the 3rd stack, dealing bonus true damage on top of Condemn's own hit
Condemn only applies a stack but never itself triggers/consumes the proc; the proc only fires on the 3rd basic attack
quotes: '''Vayne's''' {{tip|basic attacks}} {{tip|on-hit}} and ''{{ai|Condemn|Vayne}}'' apply a {{tip|stack}} of ''Silver Bolts'' for {{fd|3.5}} seconds, refreshing on subsequent applications, expiring upon attacking a new enemy, and stacking up to 3 times.

unsettled.question: Should Final Hour (R) be assumed pre-cast (already active/opener) or cast during the 15s window, given its long cooldown (70-100s) and cost, affecting how many seconds of the AD buff and Tumble CDR are actually available?
options: Cast R at the very start of the fight, consuming cast time/none but immediately granting buffs for the rest of the 15s
Treat R as already active before the timer starts (a pre-fight opener), so the full buff duration and CDR apply throughout

proposal: Open by casting Final Hour (R) for the bonus AD self-buff and Tumble cooldown reduction, since it has no cast time and immediately boosts subsequent attacks and Q casts.
Cast Tumble (Q) as the first ability to arm the next basic attack with bonus physical damage and reset the attack timer; then follow with basic attacks.

Weave Tumble again whenever its (Final Hour-reduced) cooldown is up, using it to reset the attack timer and add another empowered-attack instance, since it also applies a Silver Bolts stack via the resulting attack.
Auto-attack continuously between Q casts; every 3rd on-hit application (from attacks and/or Condemn) consumes Silver Bolts stacks for bonus true damage based on target max HP.
Cast Condemn (E) on cooldown when it does not interrupt the auto-attack/Tumble rhythm, both for its own physical damage and to feed a Silver Bolts stack.
Prioritize mana-cost management (Q/E/R all cost mana) so casts are not blocked mid-fight; if mana runs low, favor basic attacks (free) and Tumble resets over Condemn.
questions: Should Final Hour be treated as pre-active before the timer starts, or must its cast (and mana cost) be counted inside the 15s window?
Is there terrain behind the dummy for Condemn's collision bonus, or should the sim assume open ground with only the base Condemn hit?
Given Tumble's cooldown (2-6s, further reduced under R) versus its animation-locked next-attack delay, how many Tumble casts realistically fit in 15s without wasting basic-attack uptime?
Does the simulator model Condemn's 0.25s cast time and travel time as attack-timer-blocking, affecting how tightly it can be weaved between autos?
